subject: Quantitative Aptitude
description: Mean, median, mode, range, variance, standard deviation, weighted mean

questions.explanation: Sum = 12+14+16+18+20 = 80. Mean = 80/5 = 16. Distractor 14 picks the second value. Distractor 17 takes (12+20)/2 + 1, an averaging error. Distractor 18 picks the fourth value. For an evenly-spaced sequence the mean equals the middle value.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.explanation: Median = middle value of sorted list. Already sorted; 7 values → middle = 4th value = 15. Distractor 12 picks the 3rd value. Distractor 16 = (12+20)/2, treating it like an even-length list. Distractor 20 picks the 5th value.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.explanation: Mode = most frequent value. Counts — 7 appears 2×; 11 appears 3×; others 1×. Mode = 11. Distractor 7 = 2nd most frequent. Distractor 9 = the median, not the mode. Distractor 10 = a randomly visible middle value.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: The RANGE of the data 18, 22, 14, 30, 25, 19 is:
questions.explanation: Range = max − min = 30 − 14 = 16. Distractor 12 = 30 − 18 (used 2nd-smallest). Distractor 44 = 30 + 14 (added instead of subtracted). Distractor 30 = the maximum value alone.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: The mean of 5 numbers is 18. If a 6th number is added and the new mean becomes 20, the 6th number is:
questions.explanation: Original sum = 5 × 18 = 90. New sum = 6 × 20 = 120. Sixth number = 120 − 90 = 30. Distractor 22 = old mean + 4 (rough adjustment). Distractor 20 = the new mean itself. Distractor 25 = average of 20 and 30.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Which measure of central tendency is most affected by EXTREME (outlier) values?
questions.explanation: Mean uses every value, so a single very large or small number shifts it sharply. Median uses position only, mode uses frequency only — both are robust to outliers. Range is a measure of spread, not central tendency. Examples: mean income vs median income — outliers (a few billionaires) push mean far above median.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.explanation: Standard deviation measures spread from the mean. All 5 values equal the mean (4), so each deviation is 0; SD = 0. Distractor 4 is the mean itself, not the SD. Distractor 1 reflects the misconception that SD must be at least 1. Distractor 2 is 4/2, an arbitrary guess. SD = 0 if and only if all values are identical.
